label: Equal Vision Records
lede: A New York guitarist who had played with Zack de la Rocha built a band out of Vedic scripture, a school bus turned temple and fistfights with anti-Krishna flyer crews, then left it all to become a monk in India.

eras.title: Out of Inside Out
eras.text: Vic DiCara had played bass in Beyond, guitar in Inside Out next to Zack de la Rocha, and guitar in Ray Cappo's Shelter. In 1991 he started a New York band that would put Krishna consciousness at the front of every song, the way the Cro-Mags and Antidote had only hinted at.

years.src: Wikipedia: 108 (band) · Last.fm · The Vinyl Factory · Punknews
years.h: Vic DiCara starts 108 in New York City
years.p: Hare Krishna devotee Vic DiCara (Vraja Kishor das), fresh from Inside Out and Shelter, forms 108, named for the 108 beads on a japa mala. A self-released demo follows the same year.
years.xp:
The Vinyl Factory's history of Krishnacore says DiCara had written the title song of Inside Out's only record as a Krishna-conscious anthem before he ever started 108. With 108 he went further: the lyrics leaned so hard on Vedic texts that the first album came with a glossary.

Punknews later reported that DiCara was serving as a temple president in New Jersey while playing in 108 and translating Sanskrit scripture on the side.

eras.title: A temple on wheels
eras.text: With Rob Fish finally committed and Equal Vision Records behind them, 108 spent 1993 and 1994 on the road with Shelter in a bus that doubled as a temple. Their drummer later called them a very militant band, and there were fights to prove it.

years.src: No Echo (Rob Fish, 2020) · Discogs · The Vinyl Factory
years.h: Holyname: 108's debut on Equal Vision, pressed as one track
years.p: 108's first album comes out on Equal Vision Records. A pressing error put the whole CD on a single 43-minute track, per Discogs, and the lyrics needed a glossary in the liner notes.
years.xp:
Discogs credits list sessions at The Station in Maryland, going back to December 1991. Rob Fish told No Echo he was in the studio for maybe two hours, singing over music built by Vic DiCara and a drummer named Zach from Worlds Collide.

The Vinyl Factory's Colin Helb calls the record heavy, intense and powerful.

years.src: No Echo: Rob Fish on Holyname (2020)
years.h: Rob Fish's first 108 show: Unisound, Reading, Pennsylvania
years.p: After skipping 108's first tour date in September 1992, Ressurection singer Rob Fish (Rasaraja dasa) recommits in January 1993 and plays his first 108 show on March 15 at Unisound in Reading, with Shelter.
years.xp:
Fish told No Echo that Vic DiCara called him after 108's first show, in Atlantic City with Ressurection. Fish hesitated because he felt he didn't fit in philosophically, and simply didn't turn up for the September 1992 date.

The two talked it through in January 1993, and Fish stayed.

years.src: The Guardian (2026) · No Echo: Chris Daly (2017) · No Echo: Rob Fish (2020)
years.h: Chris Daly joins 108 for a summer tour on a school-bus temple
years.p: Drummer [[Chris Daly|6ece778e-233f-40b6-93c2-807129660b79]], recruited by Equal Vision's Steve Reddy, joins 108 in spring 1993 and heads out with Shelter on a retired school bus converted into a traveling temple.
years.xp:
Daly told The Guardian the tour was a traveling Krishna fest, with cooking and setting up in parking lots, about the closest hardcore came to being a Deadhead. Rob Fish told No Echo the run with Shelter lasted five months.

Daly told No Echo he hid the band's Krishna outlook from his Roman Catholic parents, telling them he was touring with a band of [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]] alumni.

years.h: Brawls at 108 shows over anti-Krishna flyers
years.p: Chris Daly says fights broke out at 108 shows between the band and people handing out flyers that compared Krishna consciousness to Nazi indoctrination.
years.xp: Daly made the point to The Guardian in 2026, looking back on his time in the band. No Echo has written up an anti-Krishna flyer incident in the scene as early as 1990, before 108 existed.

years.src: Discogs · No Echo: Chris Daly (2017) · The Vinyl Factory
years.h: Songs of Separation, cut at Don Fury's studio
years.p: 108's second Equal Vision album, recorded at [[Don Fury|0bec484f-b890-4823-af64-0e48530f6f6f]]'s New York studio, with Kate Reddy on guitar and vocals and Chris Daly on drums. Vic DiCara plays guitar and bass.
years.xp:
Daly told No Echo he learned the songs from a four-track cassette DiCara had recorded alone at the band's Philadelphia temple, with instructions to use it as a template and play it how he felt.

Kate Reddy, credited as Kate 08, co-owned Equal Vision with her husband Steve Reddy. She also led Project Kate with [[Norman Brannon|fbe11657-2638-4486-8369-2157644a9031]] and Sergio Vega.

years.src: The Guardian (2026) · No Echo: Chris Daly (2017)
years.h: Chris Daly leaves 108 and starts [[Texas Is the Reason|b93c736f-a82f-4cae-9e57-a60b12d7055f]]
years.p: Chris Daly moves on after Songs of Separation and forms Texas Is the Reason with Norman Brannon. He told The Guardian they bonded over 10,000 Maniacs and Ride.

eras.title: Cameras, Europe and a monk's exit
eras.text: New bassists, a documentary crew and a punishing European run pushed 108 hard. By 1996 they had a third album on a German label and a final tour on film, and Vic DiCara was on his way to India.

years.h: Franklin Rhi joins 108 on bass, then quits after Europe
years.p: [[Crown of Thornz|e7b3e015-81fa-4180-aa7b-7bfcf821209d]] bassist Franklin Rhi meets Vic DiCara at the Krishna temple on 26th Avenue and joins 108. After a 1995 European tour he quits both bands.
years.xp: Rhi told No Echo that the outgoing bassist suggested him and the band handed him their record to learn. The poverty he saw in the former Eastern Bloc on that tour shook him, and he left both 108 and Crown of Thornz to sort out his spiritual life, later joining Shelter.

years.h: 108 filmed for the documentary N.Y.H.C.
years.p: Frank Pavich's film N.Y.H.C. catches 108 live and interviews Vic DiCara, Rob Fish and bassist Trivikrama Dasa. The soundtrack came out in 1996 to fund the film, which followed in 1999.

years.h: Threefold Misery on Germany's Lost & Found
years.p: 108's third album, recorded at Salad Days Studio with Trivikrama Dasa on bass. The liner notes say drummer Matt Cross played courtesy of Atlantic Records.

years.h: 108's final tour, filmed; Vic DiCara leaves for India
years.p: 108 play a last US and European tour, filmed by Evan Jacobs, then break up. Vic DiCara moves to India to live as a monk.

eras.title: The tape outlives the band
eras.text: 108 kept releasing records after they stopped existing. The last of them was the film of the final tour, four years on.

years.src: Wikipedia: 108 (band) · Discogs · Choose Your Heaven zine (2009)
years.h: Curse of Instinct: 108's Final Tour comes out on VHS
years.p: Four years after the split, the final-tour film and a live album of the same name appear, the album on Dutch label Reflections Records.
years.xp:
The afterlife had started in 1997, with Lost & Found's Serve & Defy EP, the collection One Path for Me Through Destiny, and a 108 track on Caroline's Misfits tribute Violent World.

Rob Fish, meanwhile, had left ISKCON in 1997 after nine years; he later took initiation in the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition at Radha Kunda in India.

eras.title: Back, without the temple
eras.text: 108 came back in 2005 with Rob Fish and Vic DiCara both outside ISKCON. They signed to Deathwish Inc., made two records with the Converge circle, and nearly lost their singer over what the band still meant.

years.h: 108 re-form; Hellfest collapses, Philadelphia gets the shows
years.p: 108 re-form in August 2005 with Trivikrama Dasa and drummer Tom Hogan. Their Hellfest comeback is scrapped when Hellfest 2005 is cancelled over legal issues, so they play Philadelphia instead.
years.xp:
Vic DiCara told Punknews his eight years inside the Hare Krishna institutions taught him that organized religion was not what moved him. Rob Fish said the spiritual inspiration was the same but the external and social side had changed dramatically.

In 2006 Equal Vision collected the 1990s catalog on the two-disc Creation. Sustenance. Destruction., and the band self-released Oneoeight, a demo EP.

q: Emotionally, it is the heaviest record we have ever created.
years.src: Punknews interview (2007) · Discogs · Wikipedia: A New Beat from a Dead Heart
years.h: A New Beat from a Dead Heart, made in a week with Kurt Ballou
years.p: 108's first album in eleven years comes out on Deathwish, recorded in about six days in February 2007 at [[Kurt Ballou|1e922902-2cb9-499f-aeb5-9a8c51dd0df0]]'s GodCity studio in Salem, Massachusetts.
years.xp: Discogs credits Tom Hogan on drums and both Trivikrama Dasa and Tim Cohen on bass. The band had signed to Deathwish, run by Converge's [[Jacob Bannon|d5c2a3e1-a52a-4af6-8e3f-aa2c4dc69af7]], in January 2007.

years.h: Rob Fish quits 108, then comes back by September
years.p: Rob Fish announces he is leaving 108, saying he can't find his place in it after his personal evolution. By September 2010 he has rejoined.
years.xp: Lambgoat ran the news as a breakup. Vic DiCara answered that 108 would carry on without a replacement and do something very different, but it never came to that.

years.h: 18.61: a Bhagavad Gita verse, catalog number DWI108
years.p: 108's fifth album, named for chapter 18, verse 61 of the Bhagavad Gita, comes out on Deathwish with Mike Justian on drums, Tim Cohen on bass and Jacob Bannon guesting.
years.xp: It was recorded in Boston in February 2009 with producer Alex Garcia-Rivera and mixed by Kurt Ballou. Deathwish gave it the catalog number DWI108.

eras.title: Anniversaries and old friends
eras.text: Twenty years on, 108 started playing the old albums in full and bringing back the people who made them. Kate Reddy came home first.

years.h: Kate Reddy rejoins 108 for three nights and four sets
years.p: 108 play Cambridge's Middle East, then Flemington, New Jersey on May 21, Kate Reddy's first show with them in 20 years, then two sets at Brooklyn's Saint Vitus, each built around a different album.

years.h: Vic DiCara's memoir Train Wrecks & Transcendence
years.p: Vic DiCara publishes Train Wrecks & Transcendence: A Collision of Hardcore & Hare Krishna, his account of the Inside Out, Shelter and 108 years. Deathwish reissues Threefold Misery on vinyl the same year.
years.xp: Norman Brannon's Anti-Matter later described DiCara as having left ISKCON after about a decade as a monk and working as a Vedic astrologer and Sanskrit translator in Japan.

years.h: Songs of Separation at 25: two Brooklyn nights, 108 copies
years.p: 108 mark Songs of Separation's 25th anniversary with two New York shows, including Brooklyn Bazaar. Equal Vision's remastered blue vinyl, limited to 108 copies, is sold only at the shows.

years.h: 108 and [[Judge|3827fbb6-e219-4e2d-9af8-35cc9a7d8d8e]] share a Northeast run
years.p: 108 co-headline with Judge at Boston's Middle East, Brooklyn Monarch and the Space Ballroom in Hamden, Connecticut.
